defaults.permitted_development: A two-storey extension in England has a much narrower permitted development route than a single-storey project. Rear two-storey additions can sometimes fit within Class A, but side or wraparound schemes often need planning permission. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.

rules.height_rules: No part should exceed the highest part of the existing roof, and the eaves should not be higher than the existing eaves.
rules.depth_rules: A two-storey rear extension should usually project no more than 3m beyond the original rear wall and must not sit within 7m of the boundary opposite that rear wall if it is to stay within permitted development.
rules.boundary_rules: Upper floors intensify overlooking and overbearing concerns. Councils look closely at rear-boundary separation, side-window positions and the effect on neighbouring gardens and habitable rooms. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.
rules.roof_rules: The roof pitch should, so far as practicable, match the existing house and the extension should stay clearly behind the principal elevation. Bulky side roofs and forward projection are common reasons permission is needed.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should match or closely relate to the existing house so the upper floor does not look like a separate block perched behind or beside the dwelling. restrictions.conservation_area: Extensions in a conservation area often need a tighter design and siting assessment, especially on visible elevations or where the scheme would alter roof form, frontage or the rhythm of the street.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually required for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be needed.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can remove the usual householder fallback route in selected streets or heritage areas, so check the property's designation before relying on permitted development.
